sources.outlet: US EPA Region 7, State Review Framework Round 5 report, Missouri
sources.quote: Facilities with a pattern of repeated noncompliance were continually issued LOWs and NOVs, remaining out of compliance with no referral for formal enforcement.
sources.searcher_note: EPA audit of Missouri's Clean Water Act program (FY2024 review year) finds repeat violators left without formal enforcement; also says Missouri under-flags SNC in the national database. Names Missouri, not the 97 or 433 counts.

sources.outlet: US EPA Region 5, State Review Framework Round 4 report, Ohio
sources.quote: Ohio EPA will reduce by 30% the number of facilities in effluent SNC for 4 or more quarters.
sources.searcher_note: EPA audit of Ohio's Clean Water Act program (FY2022 review year): 0 of 18 majors got timely formal action for SNC; only 13 of 26 files had appropriate enforcement; Ohio commits to cut long-running effluent SNC facilities (baseline: Region 5 Top 200 list). Names Ohio, not the 68 or 433 counts.

sources.quote: shrinking funds, plummeting staff levels, declining enforcement metrics, and a corresponding rise in significant noncompliance with the Clean Water Act
sources.searcher_note: Pattern: EPA Region 7 (Iowa, Kansas, Missouri, Nebraska) Clean Water Act enforcement decline and rising SNC. Missouri named only as a Region 7 state.

sources.quote: nearly 11,000 facilities significantly exceeded their permit limits and illegally discharged pollutants into nearby waters in 2018.
sources.searcher_note: Pattern: national significant noncompliance under NPDES; GAO also flags that only about 70% of facilities have complete enough data to track compliance.

sources.quote: Coordinated with NPDES authorized states to achieve an FY 2023 SNC rate of 9.3% from an FY 2018 baseline of 20.3%.
sources.searcher_note: Counterpoint: EPA reports the national NPDES SNC rate fell by more than half, 2018 to 2023. Different measure (one-year SNC rate), not chronic multi-year violators without formal action.

notes: No news or report found that counts permits in chronic violation over 2020-2026 without formal enforcement, or the 433 / Missouri 97 / Ohio 68 figures. Closest are EPA's own State Review Framework audits of Missouri (May 2026) and Ohio (Jan 2025), which find repeat violators left without formal enforcement in each state; the Missouri audit also says Missouri does not consistently flag SNC in the national database, which bears on the lead's watch-out (state actions that never reach EPA's system). Page quotes from the two SRF PDFs were copied from the PDF text layer. No local news coverage found for either state.
